passages.note: Interview: wants to make pre-K and early care affordable, which shows the pro-public-support side but names no income reach (universal vs. low/middle-income vs. threshold) and no provider grants.
Current-campaign affordability page promises 'expanding help with childcare' with no scope, mechanism, or income reach; page itself is undated beyond the 2026 campaign.

Debate answer on school accountability: childcare should be a place kids learn and the state should move toward early childhood education; speaks to quality/early education, not how far public money reaches.
Biographical remark that his parents could not afford childcare and few can today; a diagnosis naming no policy.

rows.reasoning: Becerra says he would 'make pre -K and early care affordable' and promises 'expanding help with childcare', which places him on the side of more public support, but nothing separates 'publicly funded universal childcare ... regardless of income' from 'significantly expanding subsidies and provider grants ... for low- and middle-income families' or from targeted threshold-based credits with provider training and facility grants. No passage names an income reach, a universal programme, or provider grants.
